use_case_summary: Customer builds consumer-facing financial assistant (chat + doc ingestion) plus high-throughput embeddings for search and reranking across regulatory markets. Need consistent p95/p99 latency guarantees for chat; bulk embedding jobs overnight; rerank pipelines at sub-second latency for top-K retrieval.
notes:
- Background: Aurora Strata is a large fintech building a multi-product assistant (client onboarding, transaction search, compliance summarization).
- Why Redwood: interested in Dedicated capacity to meet predictable throughput and strict residency/SLA needs; current proof-of-concept with other vendors shows variability at scale.
- Multi-region plan: want reserved GPU pools in us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1. Primary traffic in us-west-2 (45%), failover to us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
- Sizing ask: initial reserved pool target = 40 GPUs (mix H100:A100 preference) distributed as 20(us-west-2)/12(us-east-1)/8(eu-west-1). Request headroom 30% for failover and maintenance windows (customer asks for guidance on 30% vs 50%).
- Throughput/SLOs: chat p95 target <120ms (token latency), p99 <300ms; sustained throughput target 900k tokens/min across pools during peak; embedding batch throughput: 2M vectors/day; reranking p95 <250ms.
- Fallback/routing: need automatic cross-region failover within 5s for session affinity; policy: region-pref -> tiered fallback (dedicated pool -> hosted compat) for emergency.
- SLA negotiation points: uptime definition (exclude planned maintenance windows), credit calculation granularity (per-minute vs daily), maintenance blackout windows for market close, accelerated incident paging for severity-1. Customer pushing for 99.95% SLA with financial credits.
- Security/compliance: must support SSO (SAML), customer-managed KMS, tenant-level audit logs, retention controls, EU data residency for EU customer subset.
- Pilot plan: 6-week dedicated pilot: week 1 infra + networking (VPC peering, routes), week 2 model onboarding + quantization tests, week 3 baseline perf tests, week 4 stress + failover drills (simulate us-west outage), week 5 SLO tuning, week 6 security pen-test + ops runbook handoff.
- Measured tests requested: 95/99 latency curves by seq length (32/128/512), token-per-second sustained at 1h intervals, KV cache hit improvement projected for customer prompt patterns.
- Pricing/contract asks: reserved monthly commit with ability to burst to hosted at pre-negotiated rates; option for annual true-up. Wants clear unit economics view: $/1k tokens, $/embed, $/GPU-hr.
- Internal champions: CTO (Lena Voss) cares about resilience and cost predictability; Head of ML infra (Arjun Patel) cares about kernel selection, quantization, and caching strategies.
- Quotes from calls: "we need predictable tail latency when markets open — can't have spikes at 9:30am PT"; "if you can show 30% headroom is sufficient, procurement moves fast".
- Current timeline: security review in progress (sec team to deliver findings by 2026-03-12). CRON: procurement expects decision in April if pilot successful.
- Stubs: pricing deck (drive), architecture diagram (drive), SLA draft (shared Google doc).
